name: TotalEnergies

summary.text: TotalEnergies is a French oil and gas company, known as Total until a 2021 name change. A 2021 peer-reviewed study in Global Environmental Change by Christophe Bonneuil, Pierre-Louis Choquet and Benjamin Franta traced the company's responses to global warming from 1971, when its in-house magazine Total Information published an article linking fossil fuel burning to rising atmospheric CO2, through stages the authors describe as awareness, preparation, denial and delay. In January 2021 Total announced it would not renew its membership of the American Petroleum Institute, citing differences on climate policy. On 23 October 2025 the Paris Judicial Court found that certain climate-related statements on the company's French consumer website constituted misleading commercial practices, while rejecting most of the claims brought by Greenpeace France, Friends of the Earth France and Notre Affaire à Tous.

facts.claim: In 1971, issue 47 of Total's in-house magazine Total Information carried an article titled 'Atmospheric pollution and climate' by geographer François Durand-Dastès, which linked fossil fuel burning to rising carbon dioxide and projected that CO2 concentrations would reach 400 parts per million around 2010. The article was identified in a 2021 study in Global Environmental Change by Christophe Bonneuil, Pierre-Louis Choquet and Benjamin Franta.
facts.quote: In that year, the company's magazine, Total Information, contained an article entitled "Atmospheric pollution and climate" written by François Durand-Dastès, a geographer specialized in climate change.

sources.title: Science Vs Lobbying: Total, Elf and Climate Change
Early warnings and emerging accountability: Total's responses to global warming, 1971–2021

facts.claim: The 2021 Global Environmental Change study (vol. 71, article 102386) describes Total's responses to global warming over five decades as passing through stages of awareness, preparation, denial and delay. Co-author Christophe Bonneuil said French oil companies took part in efforts to cast doubt on climate science at least between 1987 and 1994, and that Total recognised the seriousness of IPCC reports only in the mid-2000s.
facts.quote: Bonneuil also said French oil companies took part in this effort at least between 1987 and 1994, and that Total "truly recognized the 'seriousness'" of IPCC reports only in the mid-2000s

facts.claim: On 15 January 2021 Total announced it would not renew its American Petroleum Institute membership for 2021. The company said its annual review had rated API as only partially aligned with Total's climate positions, citing API's support for rolling back U.S. methane regulation, its membership of a coalition opposing electric-vehicle subsidies, differing positions on carbon pricing, and API's support in the 2020 elections for candidates who argued against U.S. participation in the Paris Agreement.
facts.quote: API maintains its support for the rollback of U.S. regulation on methane emissions, which the Group opposed in November 2019.

facts.claim: In July 2020 Total announced its withdrawal from the Canadian Association of Petroleum Producers, saying CAPP's public positions were no longer aligned with Total's May 2020 climate strategy.
facts.quote: In July, the company announced that it would withdraw from the Canadian Association of Petroleum Producers (CAPP), due to positions that were no longer aligned with CAPP's public stance, following its May 2020 Climate Ambition strategy.

facts.claim: On 23 October 2025 the Paris Judicial Court partially upheld claims by Greenpeace France, Les Amis de la Terre France and Notre Affaire à Tous, finding that certain statements on TotalEnergies' French consumer website about its ambition of carbon neutrality by 2050 and its role in the energy transition constituted misleading commercial practices under French consumer law read in light of EU Directive 2024/825.
facts.quote: The Paris Judicial Court partially upheld the claims brought by the NGOs, finding that certain statements on the company's French consumer website constituted misleading commercial practices.

facts.claim: The Paris court rejected most of the NGOs' claims in the 2025 case, including those concerning the communication campaign around the 2021 name change from Total to TotalEnergies and the promotion of gas as a less carbon-intensive fossil fuel and of biofuels.
facts.quote: The court rejected most of the claims, including requests around a communication campaign linked to its 2021 name change from "Total," and the promotion of gas as a less carbon-intensive fossil fuel.

sources.title: French Court Rules TotalEnergies Misled Consumers with Climate Claims
TotalEnergies fined for greenwashing in its advertising in French ruling

facts.claim: In the 2025 ruling the Paris court ordered TotalEnergies to remove the statements it found misleading from its French website, to publish the operative part of the judgment on the site's homepage for 180 days, and to pay each claimant association €23,000 in damages and legal costs, with a penalty of up to €20,000 per day for non-compliance after one month. TotalEnergies said it acknowledged the decision.
facts.quote: The court ordered removal of the incriminated statements from the French website, publication of the judgment's operative part on the homepage for 180 days, and awarded each claimant association €23,000 in damages and legal fees.

connections.claim: Total was a member of the American Petroleum Institute until it declined to renew its membership for 2021, announcing on 15 January 2021 that API's positions on methane regulation, electric-vehicle subsidies, carbon pricing and election support were not aligned with Total's climate policy.
connections.quote: After the 2019 and 2020 reviews, Total rated API as "partially aligned" with those of the Group.

connections.claim: Greenpeace France, Les Amis de la Terre France and Notre Affaire à Tous, with ClientEarth's support, sued TotalEnergies in Paris over its climate-related advertising. On 23 October 2025 the Paris Judicial Court found some website statements to be misleading commercial practices and awarded each association €23,000, while rejecting most of their claims.
connections.quote: The Paris Judicial Court ruled against TotalEnergies on 23 October 2025 in a case brought by Greenpeace France, Friends of the Earth France (Les Amis de la Terre France), and Notre Affaire à Tous, with ClientEarth's support.

openQuestions: The 2021 Global Environmental Change paper itself (DOI link on ScienceDirect) should be cited directly; the OUCI index entry and the CNRS summary are secondary.
Whether TotalEnergies has appealed the 23 October 2025 Paris ruling was not established.
Reporting splits the €23,000 per association differently (€8,000 damages plus €15,000 costs in one account); the judgment should be checked.
The site's Crash Conduits page links 'Total Information Awareness' to this entity through an alias; that DARPA program is unrelated to the company.
